recent_posts.title: Issue № 13: Shade of the Lime Tree
recent_posts.summary: Learn to create dynamic forms using HTMX integrated into ASP.NET Core. Discover the power of HTMX for building client-side experiences with ease, including its support in JetBrains and how it simplifies AJAX, CSS Transitions, WebSockets, and Server Sent Events in HTML. Explore an innovative approach to building web apps in Haskell with HTMX, including the use of a new microframework called Okapi.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 12: Copying Down The Dates
recent_posts.summary: JetBrains has become a corporate sponsor for the community. The htmx community is seeking alternatives to Discord due to its inefficiency in information storage. Updates on missing.css include a new font switcher and potential navbar-free navigation. Django-htmx 1.9.0 has been released with documentation hosted on Read the Docs.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 11: Bump Version
recent_posts.summary: htmx 1.7.0 has been released with several new features including server-send events and WebSocket support as extensions, and new plugins like Alpine-Morph, Restored, and Loading States. _Hyperscript 0.9.5 brings conditional class addition and debugging aids. There's also a guide for migrating from Intercooler.js to htmx and _hyperscript, and the missing.css project is open for contributions. Lastly, the concept of Functional Web Apps (FWA) is introduced, which simplifies web applications through single-responsibility cloud functions.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 10: The Missing Link
recent_posts.summary: missing.css is a new CSS framework by the htmx community designed to provide decent default styling for vanilla HTML, minimal class-based utilities, and components using standard, semantic HTML. A demo environment for htmx snippets, demo.htmx.org, has also been introduced. The vscode-hyperscript extension now supports Sublime Text experimentally. There's also a new Python web framework called Dark Star with filesystem routing.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 9: Making The Rounds
recent_posts.summary: This post explores diverse topics including the use of HTMX and Alpine in Django projects to offer alternatives to single-page application (SPA) architectures, a Wordle clone made with hyperscript, the development of a personal publishing platform using HTMX and _hyperscript, synchronization issues in AJAX-driven applications, and various improvements in _hyperscript debugging tools. It also includes demos and example projects showcasing the practical applications of these technologies.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 8: Hyper Media Presence
recent_posts.summary: Explore the applications and benefits of using htmx and hyperscript for modern web development. Discover insights into client-side development with Spring Boot, and find resources like the new _hyperscript cheatsheet. Community contributions are encouraged, especially projects using htmx/_hyperscript.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 7: Midterm Season
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses various projects and articles related to web development, focusing on tools like _hyperscript and htmx. It also highlights a call for contributors to _hyperscript, outlines the benefits of participation, and mentions other web technologies in use, such as intercooler.js and ColdFusion.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 6: New Releases
recent_posts.summary: OpenXTalk is an open-source fork of the unsupported LiveCode Community project, aimed at keeping the xTalk language alive. HTMX, drawing from HyperTalk, extends HTML and enables features like infinite scrolling without duplicating code. The first wave of public HTMX apps is anticipated soon.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 5: Perfectly On Time
recent_posts.summary: Giraffe.Htmx, an F# library with extensions for server-side htmx usage and view generation, is now available on NuGet. Significant updates include improved show and hide commands in _hyperscript. The community also discusses IDE tooling for _hyperscript and the pros and cons of forums versus Discord for developer interactions.

recent_posts.title: Issue № 4: I Don’t Speak German But I Can If You Like
recent_posts.summary: Commspace has become the first corporate sponsor of htmx. Michael Anckaert highlighted the benefits of using htmx for a CI/CD service. An htmx meetup is scheduled for 25 Nov in Chemnitz, Germany. A new htmx library for F# by Daniel is soon to be released. A demonstration of htmx with Prolog for a dice web app was introduced. Additional resources discuss how to submit data from a form in _hyperscript and a comparison between _hyperscript and Alpine.js.
